replies.author: @howardhughes7596
replies.text:
Thank the Mormons. For measles deaths too. I lived there 81-83. Lovely place, long before the takeover. Only about 30,000 people lived there then and almost all Polynesians with some Koreans and Micronesians. Very few Caucasians, and many of those were Australian or Kiwis. 

Magical place. Very little fishing, zero fish traps. Until you’ve gone into the water over an untouched reef, you’ve no idea how big critters are out there. I would free dive off my reef and the resident black tip sharks would lazily swim up, take a look at me, and then turn and move off. But there was one skinny white tip that would sneak up on you. 

And I learned to stay out of the water at dusk after getting cruised by a 12 foot tiger one evening about five feet from shore. The things I saw there are memory treasures. I know the reef got busted up pretty bad when the tidal wave hit a couple decades ago. That killed about 30 people. While I was there one of the aianga buses lost its brakes and went over a cliff. 22 people killed in that tragedy. It was a place where you could off yourself very easily being stupid. 

Long ago, far away.
